papers.title: ClusterKV: Manipulating LLM KV Cache in Semantic Space for Recallable Compression
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have been widely deployed in a variety of applications, and the context length is rapidly increasing to handle tasks such as long-document QA and complex logical reasoning. However, long context poses significant challenges for inference efficiency, including high memory costs of key-value (KV) cache and increased latency due to extensive memory accesses. Recent works have proposed compressing KV cache to approximate computation, but these methods either evict tokens permanently, never recalling them for later inference, or recall previous tokens at the granularity of pages divided by textual positions. Both approaches degrade the model accuracy and output quality. To achieve efficient and accurate recallable KV cache compression, we introduce ClusterKV, which recalls tokens at the granularity of semantic clusters.

papers.title: RotateKV: Outlier-Aware Adaptive Rotations for 2-Bit KV Quantization
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown remarkable capabilities but face significant deployment challenges due to their computational and memory demands during inference. Key-Value (KV) cache quantization is a promising approach to reduce memory footprint. However, existing methods suffer from severe accuracy degradation at low bit-widths (e.g., 2-bit) due to the presence of outliers in KV features. In this paper, we propose RotateKV, a novel KV quantization method that addresses the outlier problem through adaptive feature rotation. By rotating the KV features to a space where outliers are mitigated, RotateKV enables accurate low-bit quantization while preserving model performance.

papers.title: VEDA: Efficient LLM Generation Through Voting-based KV Cache Eviction and Dataflow-flexible Accelerator
papers.abstract: This work addresses the efficiency of LLM inference by algorithm-hardware-dataflow tri-optimizations. We propose a novel voting-based KV cache eviction algorithm, balancing hardware efficiency and algorithm accuracy by adaptively identifying unimportant kv vectors. From a dataflow perspective, we introduce a flexible-product dataflow and a runtime reconfigurable PE array for matrix-vector multiplication.

papers.title: LServe: Efficient Long-sequence LLM Serving with Unified Sparse Attention
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown remarkable potential in processing long sequences and complex reasoning tasks, yet efficiently serving these models remains challenging due to the quadratic computational complexity of attention in the prefilling stage and the large memory footprint of the KV cache in the decoding stage. LServe accelerates long-sequence LLM serving via hybrid sparse attention, unifying different hardware-friendly structured sparsity patterns for both prefilling and decoding attention.

papers.title: HCache: Fast State Restoration in LLM Serving
papers.abstract: The growing complexity of LLM usage today, e.g., multi-round conversation and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), makes contextual states (i.e., KV cache) reusable across user requests. Given the capacity constraints of GPU memory, only a limited number of contexts can be cached on GPU for reusing. Existing inference systems typically evict part of the KV cache and restore it by recomputing it from the original tokens or offloading it to host storage for later retrieval. We propose HCache, a novel LLM state restoration method that restores LLM states from intermediate activations.

papers.title: T-MAC: CPU Renaissance via Table Lookup for Low-Bit LLM Deployment on Edge
papers.abstract: The deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) on edge devices is increasingly important. Weight quantization is crucial for reducing the memory footprint of LLMs. However, low-bit LLMs necessitate mixed precision matrix multiplication. T-MAC introduces an innovative lookup table (LUT)-based method designed for efficient low-bit LLM inference on CPUs, directly supporting mpGEMM without dequantization.

papers.title: DecDEC: A Systems Approach to Advancing Low-Bit LLM Quantization
papers.abstract: Quantization of Large Language Models (LLMs) has recently gained popularity, particularly for on-device settings. While efficient, quantization inevitably degrades model quality, especially in aggressive low-bit settings. DecDEC stores the residual matrix (the difference between full-precision and quantized weights) in CPU, and dynamically fetches the residuals for only a small portion of the weights corresponding to salient channels.

papers.title: SpecEE: Accelerating Large Language Model Inference with Speculative Early Exiting
papers.abstract: Early exiting has recently emerged as a promising technique for accelerating large language models (LLMs) by effectively reducing the hardware computation and memory access. SpecEE is a fast LLM inference engine with speculative early exiting, proposing speculation-based lightweight predictor design and context-aware merged mapping for predictor with efficient GPU implementations.

papers.title: SnapStream: Efficient Long Sequence Decoding on Dataflow Accelerators
papers.abstract: Techniques such as StreamingLLM and SnapKV demonstrate how to control KV cache size while maintaining model accuracy. We develop SnapStream, a KV cache compression method that can be deployed at scale in production inference systems with static graphs and continuous batching. SnapStream enables 4x improved on-chip memory usage with minimal accuracy degradation.

papers.title: MEDA: Dynamic KV Cache Allocation for Efficient Multimodal Long-Context Inference
papers.abstract: Long-context Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) demand substantial resources as their multimodal Key-Value (KV) caches grow with increasing input lengths. MEDA utilizes cross-modal attention entropy to determine the KV cache size at each MLLMs layer, achieving up to 72% KV cache memory reduction and 2.82 times faster decoding speed.

papers.title: HAMburger: Accelerating LLM Inference via Token Smashing
papers.abstract: We found that LLMs are extremely capable of self-identifying the exact dose of information that a single KV cache can store, and many tokens can be generated confidently without global context. HAMburger smashes multiple tokens into a single KV and generates several tokens per step, shifting the growth of KV cache and forward FLOPs from linear to sub-linear.

papers.title: MoSKA: Mixture of Shared KV Attention for Efficient Long-Sequence LLM Inference
papers.abstract: The escalating context length in Large Language Models (LLMs) creates a severe performance bottleneck around the Key-Value (KV) cache. MoSKA introduces Mixture of Shared KV Attention that differentiates between per-request unique and massively reused shared sequences, transforming attention on shared data from memory-bound GEMV operations into a single compute-bound GEMM.

papers.title: SemShareKV: Efficient KVCache Sharing via LSH Semantic Fingerprint
papers.abstract: In multi-agent LLM systems, different agents often process related queries that share similar contexts. Existing KV cache management methods treat each request independently, missing opportunities for cross-request KV cache sharing. We propose SemShareKV, which uses LSH (Locality-Sensitive Hashing) semantic fingerprints to identify semantically similar contexts across requests, enabling efficient KV cache sharing without redundant computation.

papers.title: TurboQuant: 3-Bit KV Caches with Zero Accuracy Loss
papers.abstract: KV cache quantization is a critical technique for reducing LLM inference memory footprint. However, existing methods suffer from significant accuracy loss when quantizing to 3-bit or lower. TurboQuant introduces a novel quantization scheme that achieves zero accuracy loss at 3-bit KV quantization through optimal grid search and per-channel calibration.

papers.title: PolyKV: A Shared Asymmetrically-Compressed KV Cache Pool for Multi-Agent LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems require efficient KV cache sharing across agents. PolyKV introduces a shared asymmetrically-compressed KV cache pool where agents can selectively access and contribute to a common compressed KV cache, dramatically reducing memory overhead for multi-agent inference.
